gloss: sweet red bean soup with mochi

definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sweet soup made from sweetened azuki beans, typically served hot with mochi (rice cakes) or shiratama dango (rice flour dumplings). A classic winter comfort food.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{汁粉|しるこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧おいしい。
⟦お{餅|もち}→お餅：23451_omochi⟧{入|い}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{汁粉|しるこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate oshiruko with mochi in it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初詣|はつもうで}→初詣：05804_hatsumoude⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{帰|かえ}り→帰り：01275_kaeri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{甘味処|かんみどころ}→甘味処：17144_kanmidokoro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{汁粉|しるこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{注文|ちゅうもん}した→注文する：21390_chuumon⟧。
examples.english: On the way back from the New Year's shrine visit, I ordered oshiruko at a traditional sweets shop.

notes: The お is an honorific prefix; the base form is {汁粉|しるこ}, but お{汁粉|しるこ} is the standard spoken form. In the Kanto region (Tokyo), お{汁粉|しるこ} refers to the smooth-paste (strained) version, while {善哉|ぜんざい} sometimes refers to the version with whole beans. In Kansai (Osaka), the naming conventions differ. Commonly served at ⟦{甘味処|かんみどころ}→甘味処：17144_kanmidokoro⟧ (traditional sweets shops) and during ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year). Often associated with warming up in cold weather.
